selected_evidence.requirement: Daily rotation with 7 compressed rotations configured for /var/log/inventory/app.log
selected_evidence.summary: Wrote and cat'd /etc/logrotate.d/inventory-app showing daily, rotate 7, compress, copytruncate; logrotate -d dry-run confirmed valid syntax and correct rotation pattern matching.

selected_evidence.requirement: Application can continue writing after rotation (functional proof)
selected_evidence.summary: Forced rotation twice: inode of app.log stayed 894710 across rotations (copytruncate truncates in place rather than replacing the file), and new writes after each rotation landed correctly in the live app.log while old content was compressed to app.log.1.gz / .2.gz.
Captured boot_id 6aa805ba-5845-488d-af03-a621555936e2, confirmed logrotate config present, log dir state with prior rotations, and logrotate.timer active.

selected_evidence.requirement: Node1 restart acknowledgement and changed boot identity
selected_evidence.summary: systemctl reboot acknowledged before disconnect; subsequent polls timed out/reset while node was down; exec succeeded again with boot_id 79f223b0-9008-4475-a38a-0adadc6604f8, proving an actual reboot occurred (not just a service restart).

selected_evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of log rotation setup and data
selected_evidence.summary: After reboot, logrotate config file, prior rotated .gz files, and the pre-reboot log marker were all intact; logrotate.timer was active again; a fresh forced rotation confirmed copytruncate still preserves the inode and allows continued writes, with rotation count still capped via rotate 7.

commands.command:
set -Eeuo pipefail
echo "== STEP 1: write logrotate config =="
sudo -n tee /etc/logrotate.d/inventory-app >/dev/null <<'EOF'
/var/log/inventory/app.log {
    daily
    rotate 7
    compress
    missingok
    notifempty
    copytruncate
}
EOF
cat /etc/logrotate.d/inventory-app

echo "== STEP 2: syntax check via debug dry-run =="
sudo -n logrotate -d /etc/logrotate.d/inventory-app 2>&1

echo "== STEP 3: baseline log content/inode =="
stat -c '%i %s' /var/log/inventory/app.log
cat /var/log/inventory/app.log

echo "== STEP 4: force rotation to prove it works end-to-end =="
sudo -n logrotate -f /etc/logrotate.d/inventory-app --state /tmp/logrotate-inventory.state 2>&1

echo "== STEP 5: verify post-rotation state =="
ls -la /var/log/inventory/
echo "-- new app.log content (should be empty, file preserved for continued writes) --"
cat /var/log/inventory/app.log
echo "-- rotated file compressed? --"
ls /var/log/inventory/app.log.1.gz && zcat /var/log/inventory/app.log.1.gz

echo "== STEP 6: simulate app continuing to write post-rotation =="
echo "inventory service resumed writing after rotation" | sudo -n tee -a /var/log/inventory/app.log >/dev/null
cat /var/log/inventory/app.log
stat -c '%i' /var/log/inventory/app.log

echo "== STEP 7: run again to confirm 7-rotation retention config holds (second forced rotation) =="
sudo -n logrotate -f /etc/logrotate.d/inventory-app --state /tmp/logrotate-inventory.state 2>&1
ls -la /var/log/inventory/
